title: Model-tiered fusebox and fallback routing playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a production-ready, model-tier aware 'fusebox' circuit strategy and an automated fallback routing playbook that combines per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant trip profiles. This ticket captures the design decisions, implementation checkpoints, test harnesses, monitoring contracts, and rollout/rollback plan. Goal: reduce blast radius from model/regional degradations while preserving SLOs and minimizing unnecessary routing to lower-quality fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable trip rules exist for: error-rate (sliding window), p95 latency, token-drop-rate, and KV-cache-miss amplification, per model variant
Per-tenant priority weights can override model defaults and opt into soft-trip or hard-trip behaviors
Fallback routing supports: compatible model variant, quantized variant, regional replica, and tenant-degraded-response with informative metadata
Circuit soft-trip triggers 'probation' mode (traffic throttled to X%) and runs a canary probe stream. Hard-trip immediately reroutes per policy.
Metrics emitted: circuit_state (OPEN/HALF/CLOSED), trip_reason tags, probation_rate, fallback_target, and decision_trace_id for each routed request
Automated tests (unit + integration) and chaos-suite scenarios validate graceful degradation and recovery semantics
Runbook updated and on-call escalation reduces time-to-detect and provides remediation steps documented in links
design_notes: Terminology: 'fusebox' = local per-model circuit manager that composes signals (latency, errors, quality loss) into a single tripped state

Two-tier trip model: soft-trip (probation) vs hard-trip (immediate fallback). Soft-trip opens a controlled window where only a percent of traffic is sent to primary while probes run; hard-trip reroutes all eligible traffic to fallback(s).
Signal synthesis: use 5m and 1h sliding windows for short/medium-term signals; require both an absolute threshold and a trend (slope) check to avoid noisy spikes causing trips.
Tenant override: high-priority tenants can elect 'protective hard-trip' to avoid costly fallback selection, or 'blackhole' mode to shed non-critical traffic only.

Fallback ranking: prefer same-architecture compatible variant > quantized variant > regional replica > cached response. Each fallback annotated with expected cost and quality delta to enable cost/quality trade-offs at decision time.

State machine: CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN (probation) -> OPEN (hard). Recovery requires consecutive successful probe windows; implement exponentially increasing thaw windows with jitter to avoid thundering herd.
Persistence: store fusebox state in distributed metadata store with TTL and region-awareness to enable cross-region failover coordination. Keep local fast-cache to avoid request latency blowup.

Decision trace: attach a 64-bit decision_trace_id to requests that hit fusebox to correlate with tracing and downstream throttles. Store last 3 trip events for debugging in request logs (not payload).
Backpressure vector: integrate with token-bucket at ingress so that when a fusebox soft-trips we can apply token-budgeted shedding per-tenant using tenant-priority weights.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Library and config - implement fusebox library in runtime (PR GH-Redwood/inference-runtime#1287) with a pluggable signal adapter interface
Phase 2: Signals and detectors - implement standard detectors (error-rate, p95 latency, kv-amplification) and trend slope check (PR GH-Redwood/telemetry#443)
Phase 3: Fallback catalog - extend model catalog to include fallback candidates and quality-cost metadata (PR GH-Redwood/model-catalog#92)
Phase 4: Routing integration - wire fusebox decision path into request router with safe reroute semantics and decision_trace propagation (PR GH-Redwood/router#301)
Phase 5: Tenant controls - console + API to set per-tenant overrides and protective profiles (internal RFC + UI mock in Figma)
Phase 6: Persistence + multi-region coordination - metadata store schema migrations and replication test harness
Phase 7: Tests & chaos - add deterministic simulator and chaos-runner scenarios that emulate degraded GPUs, high kv-miss storms, and region partitioning
Phase 8: Observability - dashboards, alerts, and SLO tie-ins (see metrics_to_monitor)
test_plan: Unit tests for fusebox state transitions including jittered thawing windows
Integration test: simulate 10k req/min with injected 10% model failures and verify soft-trip probation behavior and successful canary probes
Chaos tests: region isolation to validate multi-region failover chooses fallback replica and preserves sticky sessions when applicable
Quality regression: run prompt-set evals against primary and fallback candidates to measure quality delta and ensure selected fallback stays within configured max_delta_quality
Latency SLO tests: ensure p99 and p95 targets for each model tier are met post-fallback under expected load profiles
E2E rollback test: scripted rollback that closes circuits and returns traffic to primary without double-routing or token-accounting leaks
rollout_plan: Canary release to 5% of traffic for non-critical tenants in us-west-2 for 48 hours
Observe metrics and run automated canary probes (success rate, probe latency, fallback_ratio) — threshold: probe success >= 99% and fallback_ratio <= 2% before widening
Step up to 25% across US regions with mixed tenant priorities for 72 hours
If metrics remain stable, enable for EU regions under 'soft-trip only' for an additional week before full enable
Full enablement: enable 'hard-trip' policies for low-priority tenants, keep high-priority tenant overrides off by default
Rollback: revert router decision path and blacklist fusebox library via feature-flag if critical alert (SLO breaches or error spike) — rollbacks automated via infra-runbook
Postmortem and calibration window: 2-week observation where thresholds are tuned based on observed false-positive/false-negative trip rates
metrics_to_monitor: latency:p95_generation_ms and latency:p99_generation_ms per model tier
telemetry:decision_trace_id error correlation rate for faster triage
